name: dotnet-msix

Packages .NET desktop apps as MSIX: creation from csproj/WAP, signing, Microsoft Store submission, App Installer sideloading/auto-update, bundles, and CI/CD.

Version assumptions: Windows App SDK 1.6+; Windows 10 build 19041+ minimum for MSIX with Windows App SDK; Windows 10 build 1709+ for App Installer auto-update; .NET 8.0+.

Modern WinUI 3/Windows App SDK apps can package directly from `.csproj`:
```xml
<WindowsPackageType>MSIX</WindowsPackageType>
<AppxPackageDir>$(SolutionDir)AppPackages\</AppxPackageDir>
<GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>false</GenerateAppxPackageOnBuild>
```
Build the MSIX package:
```text
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \
```

For WPF/WinForms, use a Visual Studio “Windows Application Packaging Project” (`.wapproj`), not `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`; reference the desktop project:
```xml
<ProjectReference Include="..\MyWpfApp\MyWpfApp.csproj" />
<DefaultLanguage>en-US</DefaultLanguage>
<AppxPackageDir>$(SolutionDir)AppPackages\</AppxPackageDir>
```
The manifest defines identity, capabilities, assets, `TargetDeviceFamily`, and application visual elements.

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

Development signing:
```powershell
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
```

For production distribution outside the Microsoft Store:
1. **Obtain a code signing certificate** from a trusted CA (DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign)
2. **Subject must match** the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`
3. **Timestamp the signature** for long-term validity
```powershell
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
```
Store apps are re-signed by Microsoft; No production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution.

Store workflow: register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve the app name, build with Store association, submit the `.msixupload` through Partner Center; Microsoft validates, signs, and publishes.

App Installer (`.appinstaller`) supports hosted direct distribution and auto-update:
```text
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller
```
Configure package `Name`, `Version`, `Publisher`, package `Uri`, and `ForceUpdateFromAnyVersion`; update options include `HoursBetweenUpdateChecks`, `ShowPrompt`, `UpdateBlocksActivation`, and `AutomaticBackgroundTask`.

Enterprise deployment: Intune, SCCM/MECM, Group Policy, or PowerShell:
```powershell
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix" `
```
Custom update logic:
```csharp
var result = await Package.Current.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync();
```
MSIX differential updates are automatic when the same `PackageName` and `Publisher` are used.
